content: 1. Darzi AJ, Officer A, Abualghaib O, and Akl EA conducted a survey study to evaluate stakeholders' perceptions of rehabilitation services for individuals living with disabilities. The findings were published in Health Quality and Life Outcomes in 2016 (Volume 14, Article 2). 2. Pion SDS, Chesnais CB, Weil GJ, Fischer PU, Missamou F, and Boussinesq M investigated the effects of three years of biannual mass drug administration (MDA) with albendazole on lymphatic filariasis and soil-transmitted helminth infections in a community-based study conducted in the Republic of the Congo. The results were published in The Lancet Infectious Diseases in 2017 (Volume 17, Pages 763–769). 3. Stolk WA, ten Bosch QA, de Vlas SJ, Fischer PU, Weil GJ, Goldman AS, and colleagues developed a model to assess the impact and costs of semiannual MDA for the accelerated elimination of lymphatic filariasis. This study was published in PLOS Neglected Tropical Diseases in 2013 (Volume 7, Article e1984). 4. Supali T, Djuardi Y, Kaisar M, Stefanie D, Weil GJ, and Fischer P evaluated the impact of onceand twice-yearly MDA on bancroftian filariasis and soil-transmitted helminth infections in Central Java, Indonesia. The study is registered under ClinicalTrials.gov identifier NCT01905423. 5. Lindquist M provided an overview of VigiBase, the WHO Global Individual Case Safety Reports (ICSR) Database System, highlighting its basic facts and functionalities. This was published in Drug Information Journal in 2008 (Volume 42, Pages 409–419). 6. Bjerum CM, Aboulaye M, Ouattara AF, Kouadio O, Marius VK, Andersen B, and colleagues conducted a randomized clinical trial comparing the effects of a single dose of ivermectin plus diethylcarbamazine plus albendazole with the standard treatment of ivermectin plus albendazole for lymphatic filariasis in Côte d’Ivoire. The study was submitted for publication in 2017 and is under review. 7. Weil GJ and King CL introduced the Death to Onchocerciasis and Lymphatic Filariasis (DOLF) triple-drug therapy for lymphatic filariasis. Community safety studies for this therapy are registered under ClinicalTrials.gov identifier NCT02899936. 8. Bolay FK, Fischer PU, and Weil GJ described the implementation of MDA for lymphatic filariasis and onchocerciasis in Liberia under the DOLF-Liberia program. The study is registered under ClinicalTrials.gov identifier NCT01905436. 9. Meite A, Weil GJ, and Fischer PU focused on optimizing MDA regimens for lymphatic filariasis and onchocerciasis in Côte d’Ivoire under the DOLF-Ivory Coast program. The study is registered under ClinicalTrials.gov identifier NCT02032043. 10. Tafataha TT, Ngwira BM, Taegtmeyer M, Phiri AJ, Wilson TP, Banda LG, and colleagues conducted a randomized controlled clinical trial to evaluate the effects of increased dose and frequency of albendazole and ivermectin on Wuchereria bancrofti microfilarial clearance in northern Malawi. The findings were published in Transactions of the Royal Society of Tropical Medicine and Hygiene in 2015 (Volume 109, Pages 393–399). 11. Turner HC, Osei-Atweneboana MY, Walker M, Tettevi EJ, Churcher TS, Asiedu O, and colleagues analyzed the cost differences between annual and biannual community-directed treatment of onchocerciasis with ivermectin, using Ghana as a case study. The results were published in PLOS Neglected Tropical Diseases in 2013 (Volume 7, Article e2452). 12. The World Health Organization (WHO) published a provisional strategy for interrupting lymphatic filariasis transmission in loiasis-endemic countries. This report was based on a meeting held in Accra, Ghana, from March 5–9, 2012. 13. The WHO Strategic and Technical Advisory Group for Neglected Tropical Diseases released a report on integrating national programs to eliminate lymphatic filariasis and onchocerciasis. The meeting was held in Geneva on February 7–8, 2015. 14. Ismail MM, Jayakody RL, Weil GJ, Nirmalan N, Jayasinghe KS, Abeyewickrema W, and colleagues evaluated the efficacy of single-dose combinations of albendazole, ivermectin, and diethylcarbamazine for treating bancroftian filariasis. The study was published in Transactions of the Royal Society of Tropical Medicine and Hygiene in 1998 (Volume 92, Pages 94–97). 15. The WHO released a progress report (2000–2009) and a strategic plan (2010–2020) for the Global Program to Eliminate Lymphatic Filariasis, marking the halfway point toward achieving elimination. This report was published in 2010. 16. The United Nations outlined the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs), consisting of 17 goals aimed at transforming the world. These goals are accessible on the UN's official website as of October 20, 2017. 17. The WHO published its fourth report on neglected tropical diseases, emphasizing the integration of these diseases into global health and development initiatives. This report was released in 2017. 18. Fitzpatrick C and Engels D discussed the importance of ensuring no one is left behind by introducing neglected tropical disease indicators and tracers for the Sustainable Development Goals. This was published in International Health in 2016 (Volume 8, Supplement 1, Pages i15–i18).
